sections.html:
Leesburg is a town and the seat of Loudoun County, about 33 miles west-northwest of Washington, D.C., at the base of Catoctin Mountain. It covers 12.47 square miles at an elevation near 341 feet and is Virginia's largest incorporated town within a county. The 2020 census counted 48,250 residents in 16,699 housing units, 3.1 percent of them vacant.

The town has been Loudoun's seat since the county formed in 1757. The current courthouse dates from 1894 and is one of the few Virginia courthouses not burned in the Civil War, and the county government is the town's largest employer.

The Virginia General Assembly founded Leesburg on October 12, 1758, on 60 acres laid out by Nicholas Minor in six crossing streets. The Leesburg historic district went on the National Register of Historic Places in 1970. If your house is in or near the old downtown, it may carry added rules for exterior changes.

The town went from 1,703 residents in 1950 to 16,202 in 1990, 28,311 in 2000 and 42,616 in 2010, shifting from a small rural Piedmont town to a commuter suburb. Growth concentrates along the Dulles Greenway and State Route 7, so the housing stock runs from nineteenth century downtown houses to subdivisions built in recent decades. Those two kinds of house sell on very different terms.

Government and aviation lead the list. Loudoun County Government employs 2,500 to 5,000 people and Loudoun County Public Schools 1,000 to 1,500. The Federal Aviation Administration has 500 to 1,000, and the Town of Leesburg, Wegmans, the Commonwealth of Virginia, Target, Stryker and Costco each have 250 to 500.

The FAA's Washington Air Route Traffic Control Center is in Leesburg, and Leesburg Executive Airport at Godfrey Field is a reliever airport for Dulles. Relocations tied to federal or county jobs often come with a fixed date.

Green space shapes how neighborhoods feel. Ida Lee Park grew from a 141-acre farm donated to the town in 1986. Morven Park is a 1,000-acre historic estate and horse park, Red Rock Wilderness Overlook Regional Park has 67 acres and more than 2 miles of trails above the Potomac, and the Rust Sanctuary sits at the foot of Catoctin Mountain.

Annual events include the Flower and Garden Festival in April, a Fourth of July parade, a classic car show on the first Saturday in June and an airshow on the last Saturday in September.

U.S. Route 15, State Route 7 and State Route 267 serve the town. Routes 15 and 7 meet on the Leesburg Bypass, and Route 267, the Dulles Greenway, ends at the bypass. Route 7 runs about 37 miles west to Winchester and 35 miles southeast to Alexandria. Loudoun County Transit runs commuter routes to Washington and a connector to Purcellville, and the W&OD Railroad Regional Park, a 45-mile rail trail, runs through town.

Loudoun County Public Schools operates the public schools. Loudoun County, Heritage, Tuscarora and Riverside high schools serve Leesburg. Attendance boundaries change, so confirm them for a given address.

sections.h2: One bill for county and town taxes
sections.html:
Since January 1, 2019, Loudoun County has billed and collected real estate tax for the Town of Leesburg. Owners receive one bill showing county and town taxes and make one payment to the County of Loudoun. Look for due dates on the county's tax pages, not the town's.

Tax detailWhat applies
Town rate, 2026$0.1774 per $100 of assessed value
AssessmentEach January, at fair market value, taxed on 100 percent of assessed value
Who bills and collectsLoudoun County
Delinquent taxes, 2018 and earlierTown charges a 10 percent penalty ($2 minimum, capped at the tax) and 10 percent annual interest

The County Commissioner of the Revenue assesses property, and tax relief eligibility is decided by the county, so applications go there. Later delinquent years go to the county's Treasurer.

A few situations come up often.

  • A downtown or older house that needs updating before it will appraise well.
  • An inherited home with heirs spread across the region.
  • A rental that must be sold with or without tenants.
  • A relocation with a fixed date, including federal and county employees.

A cash sale is one option beside a listing. It avoids the buyer's financing and appraisal steps, though you should still compare the net, counting repairs and the carrying costs a listing would add.

The process begins with a conversation about the house and a written offer. If you accept, a title or settlement company searches the records, pays off any lien and handles the recording. You pick the closing date within what the title work allows.

Have the deed, your mortgage payoff information and any estate paperwork ready. A combined county and town tax bill keeps the tax part of closing simple, because there is only one account to check.

Ask any buyer for the offer in writing, confirm who pays for title and settlement charges, and read the closing statement before you sign. If a family member must approve the sale, bring them in before an offer arrives, so the closing date does not wait on a signature.

sections.h2: Getting an older Leesburg house ready
sections.html:
Houses near the old downtown tend to carry their age on the surface and underneath. Before you decide how to sell, walk through with a short list so the repairs you know about do not become a surprise for a buyer.

  • Wiring and panel: note whether the house still has original electrical work.
  • Plumbing: look for old supply lines, slow drains and stains under sinks.
  • Roof, windows and exterior: check anything that would trigger a lender's repair demand.
  • Permits: find paperwork for past additions, decks or finished basements.
  • Historic rules: ask the town whether exterior changes in your area need approval.

None of this has to be fixed for a cash sale. Knowing the answers simply lets you describe the house accurately, and an accurate description is what produces an offer that holds up after the buyer sees the property.

A listing can bring more money when a house is updated and you have time to wait. It also means preparing the house for showings, answering inspection requests and relying on a buyer whose lender must approve the appraisal. Any of those can reopen the price late in the process.

A cash sale gives up some price in return for speed and a closing day you control. To see which is better for you, estimate repairs, agent fees and months of carrying costs, including the county and town tax bill, utilities and insurance. Subtract that total from the likely listing price and compare the result with the cash offer.

faqs.q: Is Leesburg a city or a town?
faqs.a: Leesburg is an incorporated town and the county seat of Loudoun County. With 48,250 residents in 2020, it is Virginia's largest incorporated town within a county.

faqs.q: Who bills Leesburg real estate taxes?
faqs.a: Loudoun County bills and collects them for the town. Owners receive one bill listing both county and town taxes.

faqs.q: What is the Leesburg real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The town lists a 2026 rate of $0.1774 per $100 of assessed value. The county's own rate is separate, so check the county's tax pages.

faqs.q: When does Loudoun County assess Leesburg property?
faqs.a: The Commissioner of the Revenue assesses real estate each January at fair market value. Taxes are figured on 100 percent of assessed value.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Leesburg house that needs work?
faqs.a: Yes. An as-is cash sale means you do not repair anything first, and the offer reflects the condition of the house.
